resolutions.researcher_notes: Status not literal; inferred from prose. Egypt Oil & Gas 2020 Western Desert review lists the Salam-Abu Gharadig line in its table of in-service Western Desert pipelines. Apache/MIGA EIA describes it in present tense ('This is an 18 inch line extending 217 km from Salam Base ... to Abu Gharadig Gas Plant') as existing infrastructure. Two independent sources treat it as an operating line. Both are PDFs (200); text confirmed with pdftotext -- url_verifier substring screen cannot read PDF binary (documented false-negative).

Apache/MIGA EIA names it the 'Southern Gas Pipeline' running from the Salam Base to the Abu Gharadig Gas Plant. Egypt Oil & Gas lists it in the gas-pipeline table with a capacity in mmcf/d. Two independent sources both class it as a natural-gas line.

Egypt Oil & Gas 2020 Western Desert pipeline table row 'Salam-Abu / Salam / Abu Gharadig' gives Length 212 km, Diameter 18 in, Capacity 187 mmcf/d -- the exact triple in GEM, so this table is GEM's source. Single source (the Apache/MIGA EIA quotes no capacity for this line). PDF; value confirmed via pdftotext.

CONTRADICTION (minor): Egypt Oil & Gas table gives 212 km (exact match to GEM); Apache/MIGA EIA says 'extending 217 km from Salam Base ... to Abu Gharadig Gas Plant'. Two independent sources agree on ~212-217 km (2.4% spread); GEM's 212 matches the trade source exactly. Both PDFs, values confirmed via pdftotext.
Both sources state 18 inches exactly: Egypt Oil & Gas table (Diameter 18 in) and Apache/MIGA EIA ('This is an 18 inch line'). Two independent sources agree. PDFs; confirmed via pdftotext.

Endpoints Salam -> Abu Gharadig confirmed by both: Egypt Oil & Gas table (From Salam / To Abu Gharadig) and Apache/MIGA EIA ('from Salam Base located in the Khalda concession to Abu Gharadig Gas Plant'). Both fields sit in Matruh governorate, Western Desert, Egypt, consistent with GEM's Start/End states. Two independent sources.

Apache/MIGA EIA: the line originates at the Salam Base in the Khalda concession (Apache-operated) and 'could be used by Apache'. Single source. CAVEAT on the 100% Apache attribution: Khalda is an Apache/EGPC joint venture (Khalda Petroleum Co.), so 100% Apache overstates equity ownership; and the EIA notes the Abu Gharadig Gas Plant terminus is 'operated by GUPCO'. Flag for Update review, do not overwrite. PDF; text confirmed via pdftotext.
